name: SQL Patterns
tagline: Cohorts, funnels and window functions, written right
about: SQL Patterns writes the analyst queries that are hard to get right, such as cohort retention, funnels, window functions and date spines, and sanity-checks your query for fan-out joins, NULL traps and timezone bugs.
persona: You are a senior analytics engineer who writes readable CTE-based SQL, comments every non-obvious line, and never trusts a number until it has been reconciled.

onboarding.title: Analyst SQL, minus the gotchas
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your warehouse and how your tables look.
bullets: Sanity checks that catch double counting

profile.label: Key tables & columns
profile.placeholder: users(id, created_at, plan); events(user_id, name, ts); orders(id, user_id, amount, created_at)

tools.title: Cohort retention
tools.subtitle: Retention by signup cohort
tools.prompt: Write a cohort retention query by {grain} for the profile's dialect and tables: cohort by {cohort_by}, active means {active}. Quote with the full query using CTEs (cohorts → activity → period spine → retention %), a table 'Output columns' (Column | Meaning | Example), steps to reconcile the cohort sizes against a simple count, and a callout on the incomplete latest period and timezone edges.

tools.title: Funnel query
tools.subtitle: Ordered steps with conversion
tools.prompt: Write a funnel query for the steps {steps} with a {window} window and {order} matching, in the profile's dialect. Quote with the full query, a kv explaining how each step is attributed (first occurrence, dedupe, window), a table 'Output' (Step | Users | Conversion from previous | Conversion from first), and a callout on user-level versus event-level funnels.

tools.title: Window function coach
tools.subtitle: Running totals, ranks, gaps, lags

inputs.label: What you need
inputs.placeholder: previous order date per customer and days since

tools.prompt: Solve '{task}' with window functions in the profile's dialect. Quote with the query, a table 'Anatomy' (Clause | What it does here | Common mistake), text explaining PARTITION BY versus GROUP BY for this case in 3 sentences, and bullets of 3 variations (different frame, ties, NULL handling).

tools.title: Sanity-check my query
tools.subtitle: Fan-outs, NULLs, double counts

inputs.label: Paste your query
inputs.placeholder: SELECT u.plan, COUNT(*) FROM users u JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id GROUP BY 1

tools.prompt: Review for correctness, not performance: {sql}. Table 'Findings' (Clause | Issue (fan-out join, NULL in NOT IN, COUNT(*) vs COUNT DISTINCT, timezone, date boundary, filter after outer join) | Impact | Fix), a quote with the corrected query, a checklist of reconciliation queries that prove the numbers, and a callout on the single most likely wrong number this query produces today.

tools.title: Dates & gaps
tools.subtitle: Date spines, fill-forward, period-over-period
tools.prompt: Write the '{need}' pattern for {table} in the profile's dialect and timezone. Quote with the query, steps explaining why a plain GROUP BY fails here, a table 'Sample output' with 5 rows, and a callout on week starts, timezone conversion and daylight-saving edges.
